notes: Careers page per the page brief: the old career copy in 02 section 6 rewritten in plain English, the backgrounds we look for, application by email, and no open roles because 02 documents none. The route renders intro as the page lead, whatWeLookFor as a two-column list without titles (each item therefore opens with a short lead-in and a full stop), the built-in empty state for openRoles ('There are no advertised roles at the moment. Speculative applications are welcome.') and howToApply as a dark section with the email as a mailto link. Deliberately not said: any years-of-experience figure, a team size, salaries or benefits, a reply time, an application form (07 section 3 lists one; the brief asks for email), the old page's adjectives, and any suggestion that vacancies exist. TFE731 is listed by designation only and not described as a turboprop; the old site's heading lumps it with the TPE331/T76 under Turboprop. British English, no dashes, nothing left to fill in.
clientToConfirm: Open roles: 02 section 6 documents no vacancies, so openRoles is empty and the page shows the built-in line 'There are no advertised roles at the moment. Speculative applications are welcome.' For any role to advertise, supply a title, a location and two or three sentences.

Employment form: confirm whether the company hires employees, engages freelance or associate consultants per engagement, or both, and whether roles are based in Zug, at client sites or remote. The page says the work happens at the shop and, between site visits, from Zug.

Backgrounds: the three named (engine shop, airline engineering, lessor technical) follow the page brief. Confirm whether to add others, for example OEM field service, MRO customer support, records and CAMO, or defence sustainment for the military and government line.

Engine families: the page names the families from 02 section 4 and says depth on one counts for more than a line on each. Confirm the priority families for hiring, for example LEAP for new-generation work.

Languages: English is described as essential and German as useful. The team's languages are not documented (01 section 9, question 6). Confirm the requirement and whether French or Polish should be mentioned.

Small firm: the title describes the company as a small consultancy. Team-size signals conflict (commercial register: one person; Swiss Aerospace Cluster directory: 4; LinkedIn: 11 to 50). Confirm the description, as also flagged in about.json.

Travel: the page says table inspections, test-cell runs and redeliveries are attended in person, wherever the engine is, and that the work between visits is done from Zug (the same sentence as about.json). Confirm the expected share of travel.
Independence line: the page repeats that the company is not owned by an MRO, lessor or OEM and works for the client alone, as on the About page and in the footer. Approve the wording here too.

metaDescription: Careers at Flight Hour Solution, an independent engine consultancy in Zug. Engine shop, airline engineering and lessor technical people welcome. Apply by email.
title: Join a small engine consultancy in Zug
intro: We manage shop visits and lease returns for airlines, lessors and governments. Engine shop, airline engineering and lessor technical backgrounds are all welcome.
whatWeLookFor: Engine shop experience. You have worked in an engine overhaul or repair shop, on the shop floor, in the test cell, in planning or in customer support, and you know what happens at a table inspection, a borescope review and a scrap review.

Airline engineering experience. You have worked in powerplant engineering, removal planning or engine records for an operator, and you have been on the airline's side of a workscope review, an invoice or an MRO contract.

Lessor technical experience. You have managed engines through a lease as a technical asset manager: maintenance reserves, redelivery conditions, back-to-birth records, mid-term inspections and the disputes that follow when a shop visit comes early.
Depth on the engines we work on: CFM56, LEAP, V2500, PW4000, Honeywell APU 131-9A/-9B/-9D, TPE331/T76 and TFE731. Real depth on one family counts for more than a line on each.

Plain English and sound numbers. What we deliver is a report, a workscope comment or a negotiating position that a client will act on. You can explain a finding in a paragraph and defend every figure in it.

Comfort with independence. We are not owned by an MRO, lessor or OEM and we work for the client alone. That sometimes means telling a shop, a manufacturer or the other side of a lease something it would rather not hear, politely and with the evidence.
Readiness to travel. Table inspections, test-cell runs and redeliveries are attended in person, wherever the engine is. Between site visits the work is done from Zug.
Languages. English is essential. German is useful with Swiss and German-speaking clients, and other languages are welcome.

howToApply.title: How to apply
howToApply.text: Email a CV and a note on the engines you know, the shops you have worked in and where you are based. Subject line: Application.
howToApply.source: Email address: docs/research/02-website-content-inventory.md sections 2 and 3 (contact@flighthoursolution.com in the footer contact block and the homepage contact tiles) and docs/research/01-company-profile.md section 6 (contact@ is the general address; no careers address is documented). Same value as site.json company.email and the Email channel in contact.json. Application by email rather than a form follows the page brief; the old page offered only the generic contact popup (02 section 6). What to send follows the decision criteria in docs/research/06-market-context-and-seo.md section 2 (engine-family depth, hands-on shop experience) and the people checklist in docs/research/05-competitor-benchmark.md section 6 (former employers by type: OEM, airline, lessor, MRO).
clientToConfirm: Application address: contact@flighthoursolution.com is the only general address documented (01 section 6, 02 section 2). Confirm it, or supply a dedicated address such as careers@flighthoursolution.com, and confirm who reads applications.
Subject line: the page asks applicants to write Application in the subject line so a shared inbox can sort applications from enquiries. Confirm or remove.
Reply time: no reply promise is made for applications. If the company commits to one, add a sentence such as 'We reply to every application within ten working days.'
Candidate data: applications arrive by email and contain personal data. Confirm the retention period for unsolicited applications so the privacy notice can state it.
